newsitem.title: DENMARK: OSCE expresses concern at Tajikistan hostilities.
newsitem.headline: OSCE expresses concern at Tajikistan hostilities.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on Tuesday welcomed recent peace talks between warring factions in Tajikistan but expressed deep concern at the latest outbreak of hostilities in the former Soviet republic.

"The onset of military activities so soon after the conclusion of the peace agreement severely jeopardises the continuation of peacebuilding and the course of national reconciliation in Tajikistan," the OSCE chairman, Danish foreign minister Niels Helveg Petersen said in a statement.
Petersen welcomed at the same time the recent successful completion of inter-Tajik negotiations and the signing of a general agreement on peace and reconciliation in Tajikistan.

"The chairman-in-office would like to underscore that peaceful negotiations are the only viable option for settlement of any disputes...lasting national reconciliation can only be achieved through the cooperation and participation of all political forces in the process," he added.

Fierce fighting was reported in Tajikistan on Monday, with troops loyal to Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov advancing on the rebel-held town of Kabodien in southern Tajikistan, one of two strongholds of mutinous Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev.
However, a senior Tajik official said on Tuesday that its troops had crushed the mutiny in the south of the country and that Khudoyberdyev appeared to have fled to neighbouring Uzbekistan.

The latest turmoil in Tajikistan came weeks after Rakhmonov, who is backed by Moscow, signed a peace agreement with Islamic opposition guerrillas aimed at ending four years of civil war in the impoverished former Soviet republic.
